messages.subject: Model Equation
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I have built a model using RSNNS mlp() function which has around 13 independent variable and one dependent variable. The model is working fine and I am working on metallurgical data. But in order to combine NN and GA, I need the equation of the model that I have built. I could not find a way to find that equation which would be my fitness function for GA.
Please help me on this issue its very urgent!

Thanks,
Abhishek Das
Asst Prof
Amity University, Kolkata

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

that depends on things such as the activation function. If you use the
logistic function and one hidden layer, it will be something like

METs = ((1/(1 + EXP(9.18694*((VM − 4027.474318)/3153.286042) +
12.9723))* − 3.05383 + 1/(1 + EXP(1.8487*(VM-4027.474318) + 2.55011))*
− 1.19096 + 1/(1 + EXP(3.84729*(VM − 4027.474318) +
4.11932))*1.24936))*2.303
724 + 3.733038

Here, VM is an input and all the other values are weights that you want
to optimize with your GA.

This is from my following paper:
https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=_UG_SgUAAAAJ&citation_for_view=_UG_SgUAAAAJ:roLk4NBRz8UC

However, I don't think that using a GA will give you much better
results. You could use the Conjugate Gradient implemented in SNNS
instead of the Backprop that you probably use at the moment (that's a
parameter of the function). Or, you give the nnet package a try that
uses BFGS. It also shouldn't be too difficult to modify nnet to use a
genetic algorithm instead of the BFGS. In RSNNS that will be more
difficult, as it is more complex and all in C++. As a GA I recommend you
our package Rmalschains, or maybe rgenoud. So, you could try to replace
the BFGS in nnet with Rmalschains. That should work, but as I said, I
doubt that the results will improve much.

Regards,
Christoph
